title: Scope slimming for Console launch: prioritize card set, trace sampling, and cost breakdown MVP
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: We must deliver a production-ready Redwood Console slice that provides essential visibility into model inference costs, basic tracing, and a small set of dashboard cards for the public beta. The original PRD included a broad set of widgets, deep trace timelines, and per-token cost drilldowns. Given resource constraints and engineering risk on the serving-side telemetry pipeline, this ticket defines the scoped MVP cuts and acceptance criteria to meet our beta date while preserving core product value.

Goals:
- Ship an MVP that enables engineers to identify high-cost routes and regressions quickly.
- Provide lightweight tracing that surfaces latency outliers and error rates without full flamegraph or span-level capture.
- Keep the console fast and low-cost: limit retention and sampling to reduce storage and infra work.

This ticket documents the final scope decisions, trade-offs, and concrete acceptance criteria for the Console MVP slice (dashboards, tracing, cost breakdown).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: Deliver 4 curated cards on the Overview page: total requests, 95p latency, cost per 1k tokens (hosted), and error rate. Each card has a single timeseries and a 7d comparison metric.
Cost breakdown: Provide top-5 routes by cumulative cost over a user-selected 24h/7d window. Costs are estimated using current token-metering pipeline; per-request drilldown is out of scope.

Tracing: Implement sampled request-level traces at 1% default sampling with controls to increase to 5% for a route. Traces surface: request id, total latency, model variant, and high-level stage timings (queue, compute, postprocess). No distributed span-level tracing or waterfall view in MVP.
Performance: Console pages must load initial card data within 1.5s for a user with typical account size (<=100k tokens/day) when routed to the API endpoint in the same region.
Observability QA: Dashboards and trace samples ingest successfully for 7 continuous days in staging with synthetic traffic before release; data retention and sampling settings documented in runbook.
Docs: Public beta docs updated with how costs are calculated, sampling behavior, and a short troubleshooting checklist.
decisions: Remove per-token waterfall drilldowns from launch to avoid dependency on expensive KV export pipeline.
Limit cost breakouts to top-5 routes and aggregate buckets. Detailed per-request cost traces deferred to post-beta.
Adopt 1% default tracing sampling to balance signal vs storage. Allow per-route temporary increases via Console controls (max 5%).
tradeoffs: User experience vs delivery speed: Reduced card surface means power users can't get deep per-request detail at launch, but we can ship stable, understandable metrics faster.
Telemetry fidelity vs infra cost: Lower sampling reduces ability to detect rare regressions but keeps storage and processing costs within budget for beta.
Feature completeness vs reliability: Omitting full span-level tracing lowers risk of ingestion backpressure impacting runtime SLOs.

review_feedback: Design: Simplify card state for missing data; show ‘insufficient data’ rather than blank charts.
Engineering: Add a feature flag for sampling control behind an internal toggle to allow rollback.
Security: Confirm that trace payloads exclude customer-prompt content; design will redact sensitive fields before ingestion.
